problem: Embodied foundation models are fragmented: policy models act but lack spatial perception and planning, embodied MLLMs understand but cannot act or monitor themselves, and agent systems rely on orchestrating separate modules. No single model unifies perception, planning, navigation/manipulation and execution monitoring.
motivation: Closed-loop physical agents need perception, decision making, action and self-assessment to share one representation. Naively mixing heterogeneous supervision (text QA, boxes, discrete nav actions, continuous action chunks, progress scalars) causes cross-interface interference, so a training recipe that avoids it is needed.
key_idea: Extend ACE-Brain-0 into a single 8B mixture-of-transformer model with a flow-matching action expert, trained with SSR+ (Scaffold-Specialize-Reconcile plus a lightweight Reactivate fine-tune) to unify grounding, navigation, manipulation and progress estimation.
insight: Isolating per-task specialists, merging their task vectors, then briefly fine-tuning on mixed data lets one model retain each specialist's ability. The authors argue merging loses output-format conventions rather than capability, so a short Reactivate step recovers them. The only ablation is navigation self-improvement (rollouts with oracle-recovered trajectories): R2R SR goes from 48.6 to 57.4, and RxR SR from 53.3 to 63.8. There is no ablation of the SSR+ stages or of Reactivate.
method: Architecture: Qwen3-VL-8B-based ACE-Brain-0 backbone with a shared omni-vision encoder and LLM decoder that produce a shared embodied state for all outputs (boxes/points, subgoal language, nav actions, progress).

Action Expert + Fast Vision Pathway: a pi0-style flow-matching action head conditioned on the decoder state and DINOv3 features of the latest multi-view images, giving two-timescale control. The VLM is frozen and only the fast vision encoder and the action expert are trained.
SSR+ Specialize: independently train QA/planning, grounding, navigation and progress experts from the scaffold.
SSR+ Reconcile: layer-wise data-free task-vector merging (1000 Adam iterations, FusionBench) to reduce interference among experts.
SSR+ Reactivate: short SFT of the merged checkpoint on a compact mixed dataset to recalibrate output formats across interfaces.
Progress modeling: 8-frame sequences from RBM-1M (505K samples), progress scaled to 0-1000 and generated as text, plus pairwise A/B preference samples.

Navigation self-improvement: a cold-start policy rolls out closed-loop, an oracle detects deviations and takes over, and filtered recovered trajectories are merged with the demonstrations for retraining.

setting.backbone: ACE-Brain-0.5 8B (Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct init via ACE-Brain-0), fine-tuned via SSR+; the manipulation variant uses a Qwen3-VL-2B frozen VLM with a DINOv3 ViT-L fast encoder and an action expert
setting.training_data: Spatial QA (VSI-590K, VLM-3R, GPT4Scene, MindCube, in-house spatial harness data), grounding (RefSpatial, PixMo-Points, RoboPoint), navigation (R2R, RxR, EnvDrop, ScaleVLN, SRDF-400K, progress-aware CoT samples), cross-embodiment manipulation trajectories, RBM-1M progress data (505K samples)
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB with history for navigation; multi-view RGB plus proprioception for manipulation; video frames for progress
setting.action_space: Navigation: discrete VLN-CE actions (FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN 15°, STOP); manipulation: continuous action chunks (10 steps) from the flow-matching expert
setting.privileged: none at test time (an oracle navigation teacher is used only during training for self-improvement data)

numbers_note: Spatial QA, grounding and driving results (Table 1) are omitted from numbers because they are non-navigation benchmarks; they are summarized in the results text.
results: On VLN-CE, the unified model reaches R2R val-unseen SR 57.4 / SPL 51.7 / NE 4.8 and RxR SR 63.8 / NE 4.3, beating NavFoM, RynnBrain-Nav and Qwen-VLA-Instruct on RxR SR (59.6 best baseline). The specialist reaches R2R SR 62.2 / SPL 56.2. It also gets 98.2 LIBERO average (vs Qwen-VLA-Instruct 97.9), 82.3 on SimplerEnv-Bridge (vs GTA-VLA 81.2), and RBM-EVAL VOC 0.94/0.96 (Robometer 0.92/0.94). It improves over ACE-Brain-0 on most spatial and grounding benchmarks, but drops on several driving ones.
limitations: Self-improvement is lightweight and domain-specific (navigation data flywheel with an oracle teacher, plus an external execution state), not general model-level self-evolution.

No ablation isolating SSR+ stages (merge vs Reactivate vs mixed SFT), so the central claim of interference-free unification is not directly tested; manipulation uses a frozen-VLM 2B variant and a separate VLA variant, and the specialist nav model beats the unified one.
Evaluation is simulation only (no real-robot results); some driving and spatial benchmarks regress vs ACE-Brain-0 and trail some baselines (e.g. RynnBrain on VSI).
